title: The Four Rotations Portrait
premise: A courier must identify a face on an oddly arranged tile, but it looks like scattered marks at first. They rotate the same tile by quarter turns; at the third orientation two marks read as eyes and a curve as a smile, matching the recipient, who has been standing sideways beside them.
hook: The address is a face with the wrong way up.
visible_action: One unchanged tile rotates in 90-degree steps; marks settle into a face; camera reveals recipient leaning sideways; both straighten.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Orientation can make an intended pattern easier to recognize.
gate: Keep mark positions unchanged across all rotations and use an original simple face; no claim about face-recognition science.

style_application.geometry: True 3D or four independently authored consistent 2D views
style_application.why: This is multi-faceted as multiple perspectives, distinct from polygonal faceting.
style_application.check: Verify the puzzle answer and phone-size visibility in every panel.
